messages:
Elaine: nightdash fired at 03:12 UTC — p99 latency up ~12% on canary region, throughput down ~18%. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/rt/abcd :alarm_clock:
Ben: saw that — looks like the 7f2c4ab merge yesterday touched batching + cache-index code. canary shows drop right after rollout window 02:45-02:50 UTC. :thinking_face:
Carla: can we get a quick profile from a repro? I ran a local canary repro and avg batch size collapsed.
David: running perf job now. launching bisect and a short flamegraph job.
perf-bot: triggered perf-run 4312000000-1 (sha=7f2c4ab) -- running microbench + e2e repeal. ETA ~6m
Ben: initial flame report — bigger memcpy + more kernel launch overhead. possible batching heuristic flip + kernel affinity change.
Elaine: snippet from the flame (truncated):
```
perf-summary:
  p99_latency: +12.3%
  throughput: -17.8%
  memcpy: 31.2%
  kernel_launch_overhead: 19.8%
  avg_batch_size: 1.8  # previous baseline ~3.9
  kv_miss_rate: 0.41  # baseline 0.18
  hot_kernel: tensor_core_v2_selector
```
David: interesting — avg_batch_size down because batching window timer was reduced by the new heuristic in scheduler.go (commit touches scheduling/batcher). also kernel selector now prefers tensor_core_v2 for short sequences which adds launch overhead for tiny batches.
Carla: kv_miss jump looks like eviction policy changed: cache-index now uses approximate size accounting. that increased churn for short prompts.
Ben: CI alert also flagged a perf regression on a synthetic nightly: ci-bench/perf/throughput (job 8732) failed to meet threshold. ci-bot: https://ci.redwood/job/8732
ci-bot: job 8732: throughput -16% (threshold -10%) — marking flaky=false.
deploy-bot: canary rollout paused at step 3 due to latency SLO breach.
Elaine: action list: 1) run targeted bisect on batching heuristic (range: 7f2c4ab..7f2c4ff) 2) disable tensor_core_v2 affinity on canary 3) revert cache-index change if bisect points to it 4) notify infra for extended canary hold.
Ben: starting bisect now: `./eng/scripts/perf_bisect --sha-range 7f2c4ab..7f2c4ff --metric p99 --env canary`
Carla: adding a short patch to re-enable old LRU accounting locally and will push a canary build for verification.
David: if bisect isolates the scheduler change, recommend hot revert of that PR and re-run canary. otherwise, we may need a two-step revert (cache-index then scheduler).
Elaine: tagging SRE and oncall. @David @Carla please own rollback candidate and verification. I'll keep the thread updated with bisect outputs. :white_check_mark:
perf-bot: bisect started (jobs queued 4). update in ~12m.
Ben: FYI — posting perf traces to the debug bucket: s3://redwood-perf/4312000000/ — sharing with the group.
Carla: quick note: workload that regressed is short-token chat payloads (~avg len 24). long-context tests look stable.
Elaine: thanks. if bisect completes positive, we'll prepare a targeted revert PR and block further rollout until canary recovers.
Ben: acknowledged. will coordinate on rollback PR.
David: first bisect job reported — midpoint commit 7f2c4d9 shows regression present. continuing to narrow.
Elaine: keeping this open until either revert applied or root cause documented.
